rationale: Both solutions validate rolls and use the same scoring loop over the stored rolls; B writes that loop as a slightly tidier switch. They differ in how they track game state. A rebuilds everything from the roll history on every call, using two helpers that walk the rolls (over and pinsLeft). Their index arithmetic is subtle: pinsLeft treats tenth-frame fill balls as pseudo-frames, and over has special cases for frame 9 nested inside the loop. That makes A's correctness hard to see at a glance. B keeps an explicit, commented state machine (frame, throwInFrame, pinsLeft, over), and its tenth-frame handling is a readable switch with comments on when the pins are reset and when the game ends. A does have some points in its favour: package-level sentinel errors are idiomatic, and deriving state avoids any risk of the stored state drifting out of sync. However, its error strings are capitalized, which goes against Go convention, and B also has a little redundancy (throwInFrame alongside tenthThrow). Overall B's logic is easier to follow and check.
